Implemented in `84db143`.

The response is claimed before the first asynchronous delivery step, so a second submission cannot resolve the same question. It is routed through the normal follow-up path while the claimed response continues delivering its attachments. I kept the session identity check and retained a per-attempt validity token so cancellation, replacement questions, delivery failures, and retries remain safe: an old callback cannot become current again after a retry, and a failed attempt releases only its own claim.

The focused VS Code suites cover the overlap, cancellation, failure/retry, and stale-callback cases and pass; SDK typecheck also passes. The separate display fix keeps the original pending-question text in the submitted event while preserving the expanded model prompt.

Valid, fixed in ffb6b03bd3. Each session copy now records the generation (import) it came from, and `isUsable` checks that copy's own generation instead of comparing against the entry's current one. `reload` starts a new generation and leaves older copies callable, which is what its doc says. Failure counts and blocking are per generation: a broken reload cannot turn off copies that still work, and failures in an old copy are logged and reported to the sessions running it but do not change the status, which always describes the current generation. One deliberate exception: an uncaught error attributed by stack turns off every live generation, because a stack cannot tell copies of the same file apart (fails closed). Tests: "keeps running sessions' copies usable across a reload" and "does not let a broken reload turn off copies that still work".

discussion_comments.comment_body:
🟡 **bug** (medium)

Dropping `await this.checkpointTracker.commit()` means `saveCheckpoint()` can return before `lastCheckpointHash` has been written to the last `checkpoint_created` message. Your own NOTE states the attempt-completion flow needs that hash to be present: `ToolExecutor` calls `saveCheckpoint(true)` and is always followed by `addNewChangesFlagToLastCompletionResultMessage()` → `doesLatestTaskCompletionHaveNewChanges()`, which reads the latest checkpoint hash to decide whether to show the 'see new changes' button. With the commit now running in the background (and taking seconds on large repos), the hash is very likely still missing at that point, so the flag/button may silently stop appearing after `attempt_completion`.

**建议**: Keep a handle to the commit promise and await it when the caller needs the hash before continuing, e.g. capture `const commitPromise = this.checkpointTracker.commit().then(...)` and then `if (isAttemptCompletionMessage) { await commitPromise }` so the existing `saveCheckpoint(true)` contract is preserved while normal checkpoints stay non-blocking. If this is already handled elsewhere, a short comment stating where would help.

**证据**: `await this.say("checkpoint_created")`

Fixed in `1544b995b`. The tool runner from `mcpRunner` in `runners.ts` now keeps the `connect()` promise. When that connect did not finish before the deadline, it disconnects again once the connect resolves, so a late connection is closed. The read still rejects at its deadline, and the connect attempt itself is not cancelled; `connectors.test.ts` covers this in "a connection that comes up after the read gave up on it is closed".

[P2] Clean up inherited pipes when the fallback settles. Resolving leaves stdout/stderr and their data listeners active. Reproduced: the hook returned after 1.02s, but Node stayed alive until its background child exited at 3.54s. A persistent child can keep the host alive and keep accumulating output. Add once-only pipe/listener and timer cleanup, with a test that checks host exit after settlement.

good catch, thanks!

The fallback now drops stdin/stdout/stderr (listeners included) right after it settles so the grandchild can't keep the host alive or keep filling the buffers. 

Added a test that counts the process's active pipe handles before and after — it fails on the old code (pipes stay until the grandchild exits) and passes now. Also, added a line to the hooks readme telling authors to give a backgrounded child its own stdio, since anything it writes to the inherited pipes after the hook exits is gone.

`waitUntilSettled` has no production caller left — this PR removes the one that existed (`await this.sessionRebuilds.waitUntilSettled()` in `SdkController`), and the send path now goes through `handlePendingRebuilds`, which parks the follow-up and returns `"deferred"` rather than awaiting. Only the scheduler's own tests reference it now. Worth dropping unless a caller is coming: a test-only affordance on a production class tends to acquire one later without the concurrency implications getting re-examined.

Dropped in b3cb45d, along with `hasPendingRebuild` and the settled-waiter list. The follow-up path no longer awaits the scheduler at all; a running-turn follow-up goes straight to Core's queue and the rebuild waits for the queue to drain.

Fixed in `d23386884`. The upcoming runs are no longer part of `HUB_SEEDS`, so a slow `task.list` or `session.list` can no longer hold back an older answer. On link-up the engine reads them through `readUpcoming`, which keeps one read out at a time and reads once more if a schedule changed meanwhile, so answers apply in the order they were asked. `engine.test.ts` covers this with a test that holds `task.list` while a newer read lands.

Fixed in `19e5855e1`. `ClineSetupSource.start` now calls `refresh()` right away when `link.availability()` is `present`, and still subscribes to later `up` events and `settings.changed`. Covered by 'reads at start when the link is already up' in `sources.test.ts`.
